questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: Where does data queried through a Cloud Storage BigLake table remain?
options: In BigQuery managed storage, after the connection copies each object once
In a linked dataset created inside the querying project on first access
In the metadata cache, which holds the file contents until staleness expires
In Cloud Storage, with the connection's service account reading the objects

questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: What is a central security benefit of BigLake access delegation?
options: Consumers inherit the connection's object permissions along with the table grant
Consumers can be granted the table without any direct object-store permission
The connection's service account is scoped to exactly the rows a policy allows
Objects are re-encrypted under a key only the querying principal can unwrap

questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: When is metadata caching especially valuable?
options: When a table spans very many objects or uses a Hive-partitioned layout
When the table holds a handful of large files that rarely change at all
When row-level security policies must be evaluated before the scan begins
When the objects live in a different region from the querying reservation

questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: Why might a newly replaced object not appear in a cache-enabled query immediately?
options: BigLake copies the objects into managed storage on a schedule set by the connection
Column-level security hides any object written after the policy was created
The cache still describes the object versions it held when it was last refreshed
External tables read only the partitions named in the query's own predicate

questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: A governed BigLake table has row policies, but analysts also have broad direct bucket access. What is the principal risk?
options: The connection's service account will lose its own permission on those objects
The metadata cache will refresh on every query, since the objects keep changing
The row policies will apply to the bucket too, blocking the pipeline's own writes
They can read the files directly and bypass every control enforced at the table layer

questions.topic: BigLake: External Tables with Native Performance
questions.question: A batch pipeline publishes partitions at known times. Which cache strategy gives the clearest freshness boundary?
options: Automatic refresh, so the cache re-reads the bucket as soon as objects appear
Manual refresh, called by the pipeline once the partition write has been verified
A long maximum staleness, so queries never wait on a metadata refresh at all
Disable caching and let a materialized view over the table hold the results

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: What does a Dataplex zone represent?
options: A physical storage bucket that every asset in the lake must be moved into
A reusable template of metadata fields that entries in the lake must carry
A logical grouping of related assets inside a lake, such as raw or curated
A regional boundary that pins where every query against the lake may run

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: Which zone normally contains data prepared for trusted consumption?
options: A curated zone, which carries stronger schema and layout expectations
A raw zone, which prioritizes faithful landing and the ability to replay
A staging zone, which holds the intermediate output of each transform step
A published zone, which is the only zone a listing may reference at all

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: What is an aspect in the catalog metadata model?
options: A cataloged resource or concept, such as one BigQuery table's entry
A set of related metadata fields attached to an entry or an entry link
A definition of the kind of entry and the metadata it is required to hold
A business term whose meaning the glossary's accountable owner defines

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: What is the current name for Dataplex Universal Catalog in Google Cloud documentation?
options: Data Catalog
Dataplex Discovery
BigQuery sharing
Knowledge Catalog

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: A team has thousands of catalog entries but users still cannot judge trust. What is the best improvement?
options: Split the lake into more zones so each entry sits in a narrower grouping
Automate schema capture for every entry so the technical metadata is complete
Maintain ownership, freshness, quality, and business context on each entry
Publish every entry through a listing so consumers can subscribe to it

questions.topic: Dataplex and Dataplex Catalog: Lakes, Zones, Metadata
questions.question: How do lineage and data quality complement one another?
options: Lineage names the affected consumers, while quality rules judge the observations
Lineage profiles the distribution, while quality rules record where data came from
Lineage sets the IAM roles, while quality rules decide which zone an asset joins
Lineage refreshes the catalog, while quality rules refresh the metadata cache

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: What is Analytics Hub called in current product documentation?
options: BigQuery Omni
BigQuery sharing
BigQuery Studio
BigQuery Editions

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: What is a listing?
options: The read-only dataset a subscription creates in the consumer's own project
The curated collection that bounds who can discover the products inside it
The discoverable description and reference a publisher places in an exchange
The set of row and column policies applied to the shared dataset's tables

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: What is created when a consumer subscribes to a shared BigQuery dataset listing?
options: A linked dataset giving read-only access without a per-subscriber copy
A scheduled transfer that refreshes a full copy in the subscriber's project
An external connection whose service account reads the publisher's storage
A materialized view in the publisher's project that the consumer may query

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: What is created for a subscription to a shared Pub/Sub topic listing?
options: A linked BigQuery view over the topic's messages in the consumer project
A copy of the topic, republished under the consumer project's own name
A native BigQuery table that the topic's messages are streamed into
A linked Pub/Sub subscription that delivers messages, not a queried dataset

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: A consumer needs an independent immutable copy retained after the publisher withdraws data. What should architects consider?
options: A private exchange, so the listing stays visible only to approved subscribers
A linked dataset in a second region, so a withdrawal cannot reach both copies
A governed export or replication that the consumer retains independently
A business glossary term that pins the schema the publisher must preserve

questions.topic: Analytics Hub: Publishing and Subscribing to Shared Data
questions.question: What should a publisher do before placing sensitive data in a public exchange?
options: Classify the data and review privacy, contracts, controls, and support terms
Confirm that authentication is required, which makes any downstream use safe
Move the shared dataset into the subscriber's region to avoid egress charges
Grant subscribers write access so they can correct errors in shared tables
